title: Global tensor–Hom cochains with independent coefficient universes

from.place: Proof of K-injectivity of Hom(P,I), Stacks 0A96 via the tensor–Hom cochain identity 0A90

statement: Let C be a site with object and morphism universes c and v, let r be an independent universe, and let R be a sheaf of commutative rings with values in universe max(c,v,r). Assume additive sheafification and that local equivalences are the locally bijective maps. Let K,L,I be arbitrary unbounded cochain complexes of sheaves of R-modules [def-pc-cochain-complex-modules]. Write Hom(L,I) for the sheaf Hom complex [def-pur-hom-complex] and T=Tot(K tensor L) for the direct-sum tensor total complex [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves]. For every integer n there is an additive equivalence between ordinary degree-n cochains K to Hom(L,I) and ordinary degree-n cochains T to I. These equivalences intertwine the Hom differentials in adjacent degrees. There is no boundedness, flatness or injectivity hypothesis.

source.place: Tag 0A90 (lemma-compose); cochain tensor–Hom identity used in Lemma 0A96.

proof.text: Construct the actual sheaf tensor–Hom adjunction at the recorded universes: first use the module sheafification adjunction, then the existing presheaf tensor–Hom equivalence, and finally full faithfulness of forgetting sheaves of modules. Naturality of tensorObjIsoSheafification and the component formulas for presheaf currying establish naturality in each argument. This equips the module category with a private closed structure whose internal Hom is exactly the sheaf Hom, rather than a separately chosen representing object.

Compare the sheaf Hom complex with CochainComplex.internalHomObj for this closed structure. On the (p,p+n) factor multiply by (-1)^(pn). Product projections construct both maps and prove they are inverse; the homComplex differential formula shows that these maps commute with the differentials. This is the existing HomComplexInternalHomComparison argument with independent coefficient universes.

Postcompose cochains with that chain isomorphism. Apply the additive tensor–Hom cochain equivalence CochainComplex.InternalHom.cochainEquiv, and precompose with the symmetry K tensor L to L tensor K. The generic uncurryCochain_δ theorem and the Hom differential composition formulas prove compatibility with δ. The three signs from the comparison, currying, and symmetry cancel, giving the usual componentwise tensor–Hom identification for every integer degree. Empty and zero complexes are included by the product/coproduct universal properties.

theorem global_tensorHom_cochainsOfUniverses
    {C : Type c} [Category.{v} C] {J : GrothendieckTopology C}
    [HasSheafify J AddCommGrpCat.{max c v r}]
    [J.WEqualsLocallyBijective AddCommGrpCat.{max c v r}]
    (R : Sheaf J CommRingCat.{max c v r})
    (K L I : CochainComplex (SheafOfModules.{max c v r} ((sheafCompose J
      (forget₂ CommRingCat.{max c v r} RingCat.{max c v r})).obj R)) ℤ) :
    letI := SheafOfModules.isMonoidal_W_independentCoefficients R
    letI := SheafOfModules.monoidalCategory R
    letI := SheafOfModules.preservesZeroMorphisms_curriedTensor_independentCoefficients R
    letI := SheafOfModules.preservesZeroMorphisms_curriedTensor_obj_independentCoefficients R
    let T := CochainComplex.mapBifunctor K L (curriedTensor _)
    ∃ e : ∀ n : ℤ, CochainComplex.HomComplex.Cochain K (homComplex (R := R) L I) n ≃+
        CochainComplex.HomComplex.Cochain T I n,
      ∀ (n m : ℤ) (_hnm : n + 1 = m) (a),
        e m (CochainComplex.HomComplex.δ n m a) =
          CochainComplex.HomComplex.δ n m (e n a)
